I bought two cockatiels at this shop and, as always, the service was fantastic. They gave me great advice and took into account both the animal and what I wanted and what would work best for me. You really feel like they're giving you advice and taking care of the animal.

A very bad experience. I went to this pet shop because I wanted to buy a common hamster, and honestly, I left quite disappointed.
The woman who served me, who wore glasses, was not friendly at all. She informed me that I couldn't buy just the hamster, but that I was forced to buy a complete package with a cage, water bottle, etc., for €60.
I find this quite outrageous, especially considering that in other pet shops in Barcelona you can find the hamster for around €12 and buy the accessories separately according to your needs.
Forcing the customer to buy a €60 package seems like an unreasonable policy, and the service I received was completely unhelpful.
I do not recommend this shop. It has undoubtedly been one of the worst experiences I've had in a pet shop in Barcelona.

They have no morals. THEY SOLD ME A SICK ANIMAL, which DIED.

And I waited until I had all the test results to verify that this was the case.
I went to get a masked lovebird (I already have one) and after seeing a picture of mine, they told me it was a Fischer's lovebird (???). After arguing a bit, I agreed with them; after all, they're experts. And I took the last lovebird they had, a Fischer's, what a coincidence.
The bird was already having diarrhea, and less than a month later it died from sepsis. We tried everything to save it, and it's not just the money spent on vets (more than €400), it's that you introduce it to its companion and in no time it's left alone. Besides the distress we've also suffered.
They sold us the last sick animal they had to make €85. I feel sorry for them.

I feel sorry for them. We came here because of the good reviews you have in the past, but something must have changed because I've seen other people in the same situation with you lately.
This isn't right.

I found them online when I was looking for a pet, and they were fantastic. They gave me all the necessary explanations, advice, and supplies; and all at a great price. In fact, I don't live in that neighborhood, but I go there to buy food for my "new friends."

I just saw that a customer bought "a parakeet," and the picture is of a rainbow lorikeet... they eat nectar, have forked tongues, their food costs a lot of money... but she says it's a parakeet. That's how animal shelters are... with hundreds of parrots!! Ignorant people!!... I've been going there to buy food for years. It's all overcrowded, and obviously, I don't like seeing babies treated like merchandise... but they have everything. I'm amazed that people buy canaries and other bird species... and I, who am involved with two bird shelters, Ave Fénix and Birfriends, see tons of canaries, cockatiels, African greys, etc., living there waiting for someone to adopt them. I have a beautiful canary with feathers... which I fed completely, and now I'm getting another one, so I have to go buy breeding paste. If you want birds, go to the shelters...
I think it's a fantastic place; they provide excellent service and advice, and you can tell they have a real knack for animals.
The two women treated me very well; they even helped me carry the animal I bought to the car. They were very attentive and kind, thank you!
Very good

A horrendous experience.
Four days ago, I rescued two chicks that had fallen from their nest (they were no more than a week old). I fed them with seed-based formula, and everything was fine. They were super strong and active.
I went to the store to buy more formula because I was almost out, and after explaining their needs, they told me they were two swallows and that they would give me psittacine formula because they didn't have any insectivore formula.
After four days of eating only grain, if they were insectivores, they would be dead.
I took the formula with me and fed them once before going to bed because they didn't eat at night. This morning, I found one dead because it hadn't been able to defecate. I'm incredibly angry that all my effort was for nothing because they clearly don't know what they're doing. I was also told to feed them every three hours because, and I quote, "they are babies that eat little but very frequently." If they eat small amounts frequently, feeding them every three hours is an absurd amount of time without food for them, especially since they're chicks with a very fast metabolism and want to eat every half hour. I can't space out their feedings that much.
Leaving aside the feeding issue, the service was appalling. They asked for the carrier I kept them in to show the chicks to the person who supposedly knew about birds, and then, instead of returning them, they left them on the counter. The shop was packed, and with how small the place is, if someone bumps the carrier, they'll go flying.
There were tons of birds for sale in cages on the floor, incredibly stressed. Shortly after I went in, a woman came in with her dog off-leash, and they didn't even tell her to put it on a leash. I find this treatment appalling, outrageous, and completely lacking in animal welfare. Furthermore, I find it very strange and contradictory that their website says: DON'T BUY, ADOPT. But they also breed and sell birds.
I don't plan to return and I don't recommend anyone go.

I left my lovebird at this pet daycare trusting that she would be well cared for, and I received a video that broke my heart: a dirty cage, spoiled fruit, and this is treatment that, for me, is unacceptable for any living being. I had to cut my flight short to get her out of there as soon as possible. Since then, my little one has been under veterinary treatment for weeks, fighting to recover.
You can't imagine the helplessness, guilt, and pain I felt knowing she might have suffered. Please, do not take your pets to this daycare. My experience was devastating, and I wouldn't wish it on anyone.

My anger isn't about what I spent on the canary or the money the vet charged, which doubled the price of the canary, but about the store's malpractice. Ladies and gentlemen, YOU CAN'T SELL SICK ANIMALS!!! They have to have veterinary care.
Are you going to pay all the vet expenses? Because I won't accept any exchange of animal or a refund. They are animals, not objects.
I want you to cover the vet expenses. I'm going to do whatever it takes to make them learn their lesson and do things properly.

They tried to hide its illness, which was diarrhea, by cleaning it. They had other budgies in the same condition, with diarrhea. I went to the vet, and he told me it had megabacteria. I spent a fortune unnecessarily because of their eagerness to make a sale. I've been buying budgies from other stores for years and have never had any problems. But here I encountered this.
